method: Direct view_image inspection of all identified primary pages. OCR used only to locate passages.

records.observed: Complete ordinary masculine pattern; æ-to-a plural alternation is limited to the stated single-consonant context. h-loss and syncope need lexical diagnostics.
Ēðel contracts to ēðl- before endings, unlike cluster-heavy hęngest. -end nouns and exceptional -u/w patterns are separately stated.
Complete -e masculine model and explicit hęre insertion variants -g-/-ig-. A chosen paradigm must state its selected stem; ordinary ęnde alone does not determine all hęre variants.
Selected u-stems and root/umlaut masculine class distinguished. Fōt/fēond are explicit members; their exact exceptions continue on p32.

Fōt full N/G/D/A singular/plural: fōt/fōtes/fēt/fōt; fēt/fōta/fōtum/fēt, with fōte dative alternative. Fēond normally has fēonde dative, with nominative/accusative plural alternatives. Neuter short/heavy N/A plural rule remains separate.
Neuter -e and irregular r plurals are distinct from ordinary consonant neuters. Strong feminine introduction alone does not assign all exceptional endingless accusatives.
Complete feminine short/long paradigms and documented alternatives. Glōf supplies the ordinary long pattern; listed endingless accusative exceptions are lexical.
Sāwol syncope and doubled consonants in -nes/-en/-el/-et are explicit; root feminines with mutation are separate, including byrig exception.

Full frēond table with genitive plural frēonda; fēond explicitly declines like it. This directly supports fēonda, distinct from -endra in the wīgend class. Dative and nominative/accusative plural alternatives are explicitly distinguished.

Disyllabic adjectives take the short-model endings; frequent optional syncope illustrated by ēadig/ēadges. Endingless feminine/neuter plural alternatives also named. Selected full-vowel forms must be labelled and alternatives acknowledged.
Long-model high-vowel loss differs from adjectives in -e; weak endings separately specified. No unqualified application of long-monosyllable loss to īsern.

Separate entries: īsern noun§47 and īsern adjective§57. The latter directly identifies the assigned short-model adjective; retaining the second vowel is consistent with the stated short-second-syllable restriction on syncope.

limits: Specific proposed new paradigms and actual displayed routes still require comparison against these rules and individual lexical evidence. This inspection does not by itself certify the future learner tables.
